source.title: Deep Linear Networks can Benignly Overfit when Shallow Ones Do
source.authors: Niladri S. Chatterji; Philip M. Long

record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes and simulates excess risk for interpolating deep linear networks trained on noisy regression data, testing benign generalization with a different model family and risk analysis. It does not test any listed version's defining comparison or intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical excess-risk bounds and simulation results for initialization scales. Its claims about prior studies are citations, not rows. No results compare random-label and natural-label training, width beyond interpolation, convolutional and fully connected models, optimizers, batch sizes, dropout, sharpness, or example removal.
record.test_reason: The study establishes risk bounds and initialization effects for interpolating regression networks, but tests none of V1–V8's defining comparisons. Fitting noisy regression targets is not V1's random-versus-natural-label comparison. A width-dependent upper bound is not evidence that actual test error keeps falling beyond interpolation, as V2 requires.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but omits a central conclusion: the authors identify the same conditional variance as for the minimum-ℓ2-norm interpolant, so depth does not improve noise hiding in their quadratic-loss setting. Their conditional risk bounds approach or match that interpolant's bounds, while simulations show initialization effects and a first-versus-last-layer asymmetry for ReLU networks.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes deep linear regression and includes ReLU simulations, using gradient flow for theory and full-batch gradient descent for simulations; the listed versions concern classification, architecture comparisons, optimizer and regularization conditions, sharpness, and example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scale changes excess risk; in ReLU simulations, varying the first-layer scale changes risk while varying the last-layer scale has little reported effect.

fits_no_version.finding: Under specified covariance, initialization, width, and training conditions, interpolating deep linear networks approach or match minimum-ℓ2-norm interpolant risk bounds; simulations show larger risk with larger first- or last-layer initialization scales.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep linear regression networks can benignly overfit under suitable conditions, with generalization depending on initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: In the tested ReLU regression setup, risk increases with first-layer initialization scale but shows no significant increase with last-layer scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scales in different layers can have asymmetric effects on ReLU regression generalization.

record.problems: Theoretical results are upper bounds under restrictive assumptions, and the authors state that the conditional-bias bound may be improvable and that conditions on β and m may be relaxable. Empirical evidence is simulation-based; plots provide no numeric risk values in the text. ReLU results are described as more nuanced and cover a limited setup.

untested.parts: Same-architecture random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level held-out performance on random labels.
Actual test-error changes when network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning, weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover held-out performance.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps relative to alternative measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. The original-source citations provide background, not independent tests of the listed versions. Row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not dispute the reported initialization trends or theorem statements.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting fixed random labels or compare random-label and natural-label test performance for the same architecture and recipe.
Does not sweep width past the zero-training-error threshold or measure test error as width changes.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Does not compare batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Does not test dropout or weight decay.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with other generalization measures.
Does not remove memorized examples or measure the resulting change in test accuracy.

rows.subject: deep linear networks
rows.size_stated: Three layers; middle-layer width m = 10(d + q) in the simulations
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on squared loss until training loss is below 10^-7; first-layer initialization scale varied

conditions.value: n = 100; y = xΘ⋆ + ω; x ∼ N(0, Σ), ω ∼ N(0, 1); d varies in Figure 3
Middle layers identity; last-layer entries initialized from N(0, 1); first-layer scale α varied

rows.value: Risk increases as the first-layer initialization scale increases; smaller initialization yields smaller excess risk and a solution closer to the minimum ℓ2-norm interpolator.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval over 20 runs; text gives no numeric values.
rows.note: Text describes the direction of the result; plotted numeric values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The initialization-scale effect does not measure any listed version. Figure 3 varies input dimension, with network width changing alongside it; it is not an isolated width comparison.

rows.subject: deep linear networks
rows.size_stated: Three layers; middle-layer width m = 10(d + q) in the simulations
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on squared loss until training loss is below 10^-7; last-layer initialization scale varied

conditions.value: Middle layers identity; first-layer entries initialized from N(0, 1); last-layer scale varied

rows.measure: Excess risk and distance from the minimum ℓ2-norm interpolator
rows.value: The excess risk increases as the last-layer initialization scale increases; as the initialization function approaches zero, the trained model approaches the minimum ℓ2-norm interpolator.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval over 20 runs; text gives no numeric values.
rows.note: The displayed setup paragraph mistakenly calls the varied last-layer scale α; the figure and surrounding text identify it as β.
rows.check: The initialization-scale effect does not measure any listed version. Identifying the varied last-layer scale as β correctly resolves the setup paragraph's typo.

rows.subject: deep ReLU networks
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on squared loss until training loss is below 10^-7; first-layer initialization scale varied

conditions.value: n = 500; teacher is a two-layer ReLU network of width 10; x ∼ N(0, I10×10), ω ∼ N(0, 1)
Middle layers identity; last-layer entries initialized from N(0, 1); first-layer scale α varied

rows.value: Excess risk increases with the first-layer initialization scale; risk is smaller for smaller α.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval over 20 runs; text gives no numeric values.
rows.note: The paper describes this as similar to the deep linear result for the first layer.
rows.check: The initialization-scale effect does not measure any listed version. Teacher width is internally inconsistent: Section 7 says 10, while Figure 2's caption says 50. The student's width is 50.

rows.subject: deep ReLU networks
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on squared loss until training loss is below 10^-7; last-layer initialization scale varied

conditions.value: n = 500; teacher is a two-layer ReLU network of width 10; x ∼ N(0, I10×10), ω ∼ N(0, 1)
Middle layers identity; first-layer entries initialized from N(0, 1); last-layer scale β varied

rows.value: The text reports no significant increase in excess risk as the last-layer initialization scale changes; risk is largely unaffected by β.
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval over 20 runs; text gives no numeric values.
rows.note: This contrasts with the effect of varying the first-layer scale in the ReLU simulations.
rows.check: The reported negligible last-layer initialization effect is not absence of any V1–V8 effect. Teacher width is internally inconsistent: Section 7 says 10, while Figure 2's caption says 50.

rows.subject: interpolating deep linear networks
rows.size_stated: arbitrary depth L > 1; width not specified in Theorem 3.1
rows.stage_stated: trained to interpolation by gradient flow
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical excess-risk decomposition and bound for interpolating networks

conditions.value: i.i.d. mean-zero sub-Gaussian covariates and conditionally sub-Gaussian noise; d > n
Perpetually Λ-bounded process with loss converging to zero

rows.measure: Excess risk, decomposed into minimum-ℓ2-norm bias and variance plus additional term Ξ
rows.value: Risk(Θ) = Bias(Θℓ2) + Variance(Θℓ2) + Ξ; Ξ is bounded using the component of Θ outside the training-data row span and training quantities.
rows.note: This is a bound under stated assumptions, not a measured empirical test error.
rows.check: This conditional theoretical risk result measures none of V1–V8; its state cannot be observed relative to those versions. Preserve its status as a theorem rather than an empirical measurement.

rows.subject: randomly initialized deep linear networks
rows.size_stated: Width m subject to Theorem 3.2 conditions; arbitrary depth L > 1
rows.stage_stated: trained to interpolation by gradient flow
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical excess-risk bound under random initialization

conditions.value: First and last layers Gaussian with scales α and β; middle layers identity; α ≤ 1 and β subject to theorem condition

rows.baseline: Minimum ℓ2-norm interpolant bias and variance bounds
rows.value: Risk is bounded by the minimum ℓ2-norm interpolant bias and variance plus Ξ; the stated upper bound on Ξ can be made arbitrarily small by decreasing α with other parameters fixed, and at α = 0 the bound gives the same risk as the minimum ℓ2-norm interpolant.
rows.note: The result is a theoretical bound and is conditional on the theorem's initialization, width, and sample-size assumptions.
rows.check: This initialization-dependent theoretical bound measures none of V1–V8. Its decreasing component with width does not establish decreasing actual test error beyond interpolation.

rows.subject: randomly initialized deep linear networks
rows.size_stated: Width m ≥ c(d + q + log(1/δ)); depth L > 1
rows.stage_stated: trained to interpolation by gradient flow
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical risk bound in the (k, ε)-spike covariance setting

conditions.value: (k, ε)-spike covariance; d ≥ cn; n ≥ c max{k + εd, log(1/δ)}
There exist suitable α and β; middle layers identity

rows.value: Risk(Θ) ≤ c(εd‖Θ⋆‖²/n + qk log(q/δ)/n + nq log(q/δ)/d).
rows.note: The bound is reported for a specified covariance model and suitable initialization scales.
rows.check: This theoretical bound under spiked covariance and suitable initialization measures none of V1–V8.
